---
title: Prediction and inference
guide-section: "Results"
---

After fitting, `model.predict()` generates predictions for new covariate values.

## Point predictions

```python
preds = model.predict(new_data)
```

By default, predictions are on the **response scale** (after applying the inverse link). Use `type=`
to change the scale:

| `type=` | Returns |
|---|---|
| `"response"` | $\hat\mu = g^{-1}(\hat\eta)$: fitted values on the response scale (default) |
| `"link"` | $\hat\eta = X\hat\beta$: fitted values on the linear predictor scale |
| `"terms"` | A frame with one column per model term, showing each term's contribution to $\hat\eta$ |

```python
# On the linear predictor scale
preds_link = model.predict(new_data, type="link")

# Term contributions
term_preds = model.predict(new_data, type="terms")
```

## Standard errors

Set `se=True` to also return a standard error for each prediction:

```python
preds = model.predict(new_data, se=True)
# Returns a frame with columns: fit, se_fit
```

Standard errors are computed from the Bayesian covariance matrix
$V_\beta = (X^\top W X + \sum_j \lambda_j S_j)^{-1}$, which accounts for smoothing parameter
uncertainty via the empirical Bayes correction of Marra & Wood.

## Confidence intervals

```python
ci = model.predict_interval(new_data, level=0.95)
# Returns: fit, lower, upper
```

By default these are **pointwise** intervals. For **simultaneous** bands that hold uniformly across
the covariate range:

```python
ci = model.predict_interval(new_data, level=0.95, simultaneous=True)
```

## In-sample fitted values

```python
fitted = model.fitted_values          # on the response scale
linear_pred = model.linear_predictor  # on the link scale
```

## Residuals

```python
model.residuals()                     # deviance residuals (default)
model.residuals(type="pearson")
model.residuals(type="response")
model.residuals(type="working")
```
